summary: Trace principal resolution follows declaring seats to an explicitly accountable fleet root

replay.detail: Read-only resolver; no history rewrite or projection change.

schema.detail: No registry, wire, generated-client or database layout change. Uses the separately introduced accountable root declaration field.

compatibility.detail: The internal trace_principal resolver walks declaration authors in one read snapshot and returns only an explicitly declared accountable person. Missing roots, cycles, retired roots and person authors without a root declaration return none. It never infers account owners or mission requesters. agent_person and directive_note_people remain unchanged, with their existing ask routing, own-ask authority and directive-note attribution. A root counts only when its selected intent.desired claim has a Verified full-content signature by that exact person, with no on_behalf. Unsigned, Held, Invalid, host/other-signer and field-only signatures return none. Every selected declaring-seat hop must have a Verified verdict. Child attribution rests on the person-signed root and this verified chain; it is evidence of declaration and never authority. The read has a 64-declaration budget; cycles and over-budget chains fail closed.

manual.detail: The Agent Trace runtime writer outside this repository must adopt the resolver and delete its issue #2440 host-level reviewed-principal fallback. This PR does not modify that external issuer or add an authorization input. The internal resolver can merge independently of #2390. Enabling the external trace writer's reliance on it depends on #2390 signature-candidate purity and safe pending/migration verdicts: older verdict selection can downgrade valid evidence, and migration reports Held, so attribution remains none. Provision the person signing authority before publication, then let normal sealing/judging verify the root. The resolver performs no writes, sealing or judging.

recovery.detail: Reverting removes the internal resolver. The root declaration contract remains available independently.
